rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -E '\bhonest\b|\bdelve\b|\blandscape\b|\bimportantly\b|\bcrucial\b|\bsubstrate\b|\bleverage\b|\bsynergize\b|paradigm shift' body region returns zero matches

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban in any curriculum/training surface.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No instances of 'ritual', 'ceremony', or unconstrained 'practice' as noun in body (lines 1-75)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 52 mentions 'TODO at the top naming what's unresolved' but this is an instruction about what to write in a downstream file, not a stale marker in the body itself

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 13 'test strategy authored generically is a pyramid diagram' (Rory reframe), line 38 'Authoring without invocation is theatre' (Rory), line 21 'Skills aren't hand-crafted; they're authored through conversation' (Boris direct), line 48 'ask the skill itself to name its own weakest part' (peer warmth) — AE101 voice quintet present and appropriate

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not an article; exercise file

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No named practitioner moves or frameworks cited that require attribution in body

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Consistent use of second person throughout: 'You describe your codebase', 'You are not typing markdown', 'you read the strategy', 'your codebase', 'your staff engineer' — no third-person 'the student' references

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses plain mechanical descriptions; no maintainer-only vocabulary (substrate, three-pattern, grill-me, etc.) appears in student-facing prose

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reassurance-shaped sentences appended after mechanics. Line 48 'don't settle for reassurance' actively recommends against over-hedging

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not a reference artifact

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No practitioner attribution in body; no named techniques credited

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 13 'test strategy authored generically is a pyramid diagram' is punchy; line 14-16 provides carve-out ('Quick timebox note') naming boundary and constraint

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No defensive positioning language detected; body teaches the work, not defending against vendor stories or making aspirational claims about the training

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terms like 'skill', 'SKILL.md', 'personal skills folder' are assumed-known for AE101 engineers at M3 (after M1-M2 skill exposure); no premature planting of LLM-internal vocabulary

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not a trimming edit

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The **What happened:** block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 56-58: 'What happened' block uses proper three-move shape: (1) Count+noun 'One SKILL.md', (2) Qualifier 'tuned to your codebase\'s actual testing conventions', (3) Destination 'living in your personal skills folder. Shipped.' — 34 words, no replay, lands on destination

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'Push back' (lines 32, 48, 63) used appropriately as engineer feedback vocabulary; no combative verbs (bark, order, command, whip, drag, boss, shout, snap, lecture, scold) found

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 31 'Answer from how your codebase really tests' matches body content; Line 46 'Sharpen the skill from what came back' describes actual mechanism; all headers are literally accurate

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 31 'not how a diagram says it should' is legitimate negation (actual misconception students hold); no empty negation, no deictic drumroll, no bold-label echo, no citation duplication

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No numeral-counts placed adjacent to lists; line 24 'minimum' in prompt is not a body-level count adjacent to body list

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 13 'test strategy authored generically is a pyramid diagram' — slogan is true for generic strategies (the pyramid IS what generic authoring produces); has legitimate scope

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single-file exercise; no cross-file claims with divergent stamps

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session — re-derive it per target, not per sweep.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single-file evaluation, not a sweep

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 7-9 frames as 'You author a skill... tuned to how your codebase actually tests' (aspirational capability), never as corrective deficit

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'Skill' is assumed-known for AE101 engineers at M3 (prior exposure in M1-M2); context from line 21 'Skills aren't hand-crafted; they're authored through conversation' continues earning on first prominent use

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is AE101 (engineer audience), not Agents 101 (business/leader audience); rule fires on Agents 101 only

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No confusion between persistent artifact memory and runtime context state

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Recovery instructions not omitted from body; no recovery routed below maintainer fence inappropriately

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not applicable to exercise flow structure

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No retro interview structure present; debrief compounding at module level, not here

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Voice consistent with M3 AE101; no M1 creation-joy or M5 long-running patterns imported

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 41 'read the strategy it produced and the grade it gave itself' — student reads for understanding (emotional payoff), not error-catching; no manual diff-spotting for validation

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Speech verbs in an instruction line need an explicit addressee.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 25-26 'Ask Claude to author the skill' (addressee: Claude); Line 42 'Ask Claude to invoke the skill' (addressee: Claude); all speech verbs have explicit addressee

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: ***Name* is a smell in body text and headings.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 48 'ask the skill itself to name its own weakest part' — 'name' is appropriate because the agent is identifying/producing findings, not because student is being asked to label something; context is Claude-as-actor

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All student actions (ask, answer, read, decide) stay in chat with Claude; no terminal commands or editor moves in forcing function

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No CLAUDE.md references in student-facing body; line 52 'ship with a one-line TODO at the top naming what's unresolved' is generic instruction, not layer-specific

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Zero em-dashes (—) in body; all sentences use commas or periods for separation

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 17 'Phase 1: Author the skill' (Author); Line 31 'Answer from how your codebase really tests' (Answer); Line 34 'Phase 2: Invoke the skill' (Invoke); Line 46 'Sharpen the skill from what came back' (Sharpen); Line 54 'Phase 3: Ship the skill' (Ship); Line 60 'Decide if it graduates' (Decide) — all use command verbs

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No inline links in body prose

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'Skill' (Claude Code primitive) context clear from usage: 'your personal skills folder. ~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md, auto-discovered' leaves no ambiguity with other uses

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'Agent' used for acting (line 7 'the agent drafts the SKILL.md', line 41 'The agent reads the codebase'); 'Claude' used for addressee/product (line 25 'Ask Claude to author', line 42 'Ask Claude to invoke'); vocabulary discipline maintained

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terminology used correctly: 'this session', 'this task', no misuse of 'run' as verb-agent (only 'invoke the skill on this codebase')

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'tomorrow', 'overnight', 'this morning', 'tonight', 'yesterday', 'last night' in body

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No headers like 'Pause', 'Meta-moment', 'Step back'; no sentence prefixes like 'sit with', 'let it land', 'take a moment'; reflective work embedded in action (invoke the skill, grade it)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No prompts asking student to restate what they already decided in body; student action lines decide in chat, not in preceding body prose

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 22 '~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md' uses .md extension by default

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All body content drives toward action (author, invoke, sharpen, ship); no implementation detail, administrative aside, or extra trivia

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No generic 'read it', 'look at it', 'study' after Claude produces artifacts; line 41 'read the strategy it produced and the grade it gave itself' names specific work (reading for judgment), not re-stating what student is already doing

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 59 'Your personal skills folder now holds one file you authored' — student as subject of what's true; line 68-70 forward-looking close uses student ownership

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No operational settings (working directory, mode, tool state) need repeated reminder at moment of use

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Vocabulary drawn from AE101 theory: 'author' (creation), 'invoke', 'sharpen', 'push back' (steering); no invented synonyms displacing house frames

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts use artifact-noun form ('Drop your bug after the colon' in prompt body is in prompt, not body prose); body refers to 'the SKILL.md', 'the skill', not 'typing', 'saying', 'telling'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body focuses on student's work (author, invoke, sharpen, ship), not module's position in arc; no sentences about 'Module 4 reads this skill' or 'this is the longest beat in Module 3' in student body (line 14 is trainer note, below blue-widget metadata)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts are registry-sourced via {{prompt:...}} markers (lines 27, 44), not inline blocks; prompt rules fire on registry entries, not here

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise file; strategy tie-in rules fire on Big Idea, Key Concepts, or module-level mood declarations, not exercise-level instruction

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: CTO-repeatable test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Student-facing curriculum exercise, not buyer-facing sales copy
